claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is the environment variable that sets the domain serving the Terraform-compatible API on self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes are not registered in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN may be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, so a separate domain and DNS record is not required.
The DNS record for PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.
The Terraform state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses tf.pulumi.com as the domain in its terraform login, tofu login, and TF_TOKEN_* examples.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ describing the Pulumi Cloud Terraform state backend.
